forage_use: rice straw (pual) is a poor-quality dry fodder
pest_notes: Grass host. Rice followed by wheat (both grasses) favours the grassy weed Phalaris minor (dumbi sitti) in wheat and carries over some soil-borne diseases.
soil_notes: Puddling breaks soil structure and forms a plough pan that limits the roots of the next crop. Burning the straw removes organic matter.
source: FAO-56 Table 22 (root depth); Punjab Agriculture Dept and PARC rice-wheat system guidance

forage_use: wheat straw (bhusa) is the main dry fodder for livestock in Punjab
pest_notes: Grass host. Shares grassy weeds and some soil-borne diseases with rice and maize.
soil_notes: Deep fibrous roots and stubble protect the soil from December to April.
source: FAO-56 Table 22 (root depth); Punjab Agriculture Dept

forage_use: green fodder and silage; stover after grain harvest
pest_notes: Grass host but not flooded: replacing rice removes the flooded conditions that rice pests and puddling need. Watch fall armyworm.
soil_notes: Deep roots can loosen a plough pan left by puddled rice. Large stover adds organic matter if not burned.
source: FAO-56 Table 22 (root depth); Punjab Agriculture Dept and PARC maize guidance

forage_use: haulm and leaves are fed to livestock after picking
main_pests: whitefly (yellow mosaic virus); thrips; pod borer
pest_notes: Not a host of most cereal pests and diseases: it breaks the grass-on-grass cycle. Shares whitefly with cotton.
soil_notes: Fixes atmospheric nitrogen with root bacteria. A 60-70 day crop that covers the soil in the hot April-June fallow. Leaves and roots add nitrogen and organic matter.
source: FAO-56 Table 22 (root depth); NARC and AARI pulses guidance

forage_use: little on-farm fodder; cottonseed cake is a purchased feed
main_pests: pink bollworm; whitefly (cotton leaf curl virus); jassid
pest_notes: Not a grass: breaks cereal pest and grassy weed cycles. Shares whitefly with mungbean.
soil_notes: Deep taproot reaches subsoil water and loosens compacted layers. Few residues stay on the field.
source: FAO-56 Table 22 (root depth); Central Cotton Research Institute Multan guidance
